answer: One strong defense is escalating cost per identity: the first identity is cheap, but each extra one demands a steeper refundable deposit and heavier proof-of-work. An attacker trying to flood the network faces a gale of rising fees that soon outruns any profit from fake votes. Honest users with a single identity rest on the terrace, while the harbor of shared resources stays open only to those who paid a real price to enter. Because the cost curve is public and enforced on-chain, Sybil farming stops being a bargain and becomes a money pit.
